blocks.prompt: 23. If the \(n^{\text{th}}\) term of a progression is a linear expression in \(n\), then prove that this progression is an A.P.
blocks.explanation:
Yeh aam (general) proof hai. '\(n\) mein linear' ka matlab hai \(a_n = An + B\), jahan \(A\) aur \(B\) fixed numbers (constants) hain; \(n\) ki sab se bari power 1 hai.
Koi progression A.P. tab hoti hai jab \(a_{n+1} - a_n\) har \(n\) ke liye ek hi ho.
Plan: \(a_{n+1} - a_n\) nikal kar dikhana ke is mein \(n\) nahi bachta.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: \(a_n = An + B\) (\(A, B\) constants)
Saabit karna hai: yeh progression A.P. hai.
Tareeqa: Saath wali terms ka farq nikalenge. Agar woh constant ho (yani \(n\) badalne se na badle), to A.P. ki definition poori ho jati hai.

\(a_{n+1}\) likhein
\[a_{n+1} = A(n + 1) + B\]
\[= An + A + B\]
Kyun: \(n\) ki jagah \(n + 1\) rakha (bracket ke saath, jaise sawal 3 mein kiya tha).

Farq nikalein
\[a_{n+1} - a_n = (An + A + B) - (An + B)\]
\[= A\]
Kyun: \(An\) aur \(B\) dono cancel ho gaye; sirf \(A\) bacha. \(A\) mein koi \(n\) nahi, yani yeh farq har jagah ek jaisa hai.
Dhyan dein: Proof mein sirf do teen terms ke numbers check kar lena kaafi nahi; general \(n\) ke liye farq nikalna zaroori hai.

Natija
\[a_1 = A + B,\quad d = A\]
Kyun: Farq \(A\) har \(n\) ke liye wohi hai, is liye yeh A.P. hai: pehli term \(A + B\) (\(n = 1\) rakh kar) aur common difference \(A\).

Tasdeeq: ek misaal
\(a_n = 4 + 3n\) (sawal 3): \(7, 10, 13, \ldots\)
\[d = 3 = A \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: \(n\) ka coefficient hi common difference hota hai: yahan 3, aur terms waqai 3 se barh rahi hain. Ulta bhi sach hai: har A.P. ki \(a_n = a_1 + (n - 1)d = dn + (a_1 - d)\) linear hoti hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: \(a_n = An + B\) se A.P. banti hai jis ka \(d = A\) aur \(a_1 = A + B\) hai.
